title: Taifa of Albarracín
capsule: The Taifa of Albarracín was a small Muslim principality in the mountainous sierra of eastern Iberia, ruled by the Banu Razin, a Berber dynasty of Hawwara origin that emerged during the fragmentation of the Caliphate of Córdoba after 1009. Centred on the fortified city of Albarracín (Arabic: Sahla ibn Razin), it persisted as an independent entity for over a century, navigating between the larger taifas of Zaragoza and Valencia and paying parias (tribute) to Christian kingdoms when necessary. The dynasty was extinguished in 1104 when the Almoravid ruler Yusuf ibn Tashfin's son Tamim conquered the region, incorporating it into the Almoravid empire; the date 1111 in the attestation record likely marks the final administrative absorption.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the principality's mountain terrain limited documentation to chronicle references and numismatic evidence, with no surviving contemporary cartographic boundary.
